ai.title: Add opencode/minimax-m2.7 to OpenCode Zen routing
ai.summary: Added opencode/minimax-m2.7 to openCodeZenModels in common/src/constants/model-config.ts and configured its pricing in web/src/llm-api/opencode-zen.ts. Refactored routing logic to use OPENCODE_ZEN_MODEL_ALIASES and OPENCODE_ZEN_PRICING, replacing the previous hardcoded map. isOpenCodeZenModel now accepts unknown types, checks for the opencode/ prefix or alias presence, and getOpenCodeZenModelId throws a 400 error for unsupported models. Pricing for minimax-m2.7 is set to 0.3/1.2 per million input/output tokens.

eli5.text: You can now pick OpenCode MiniMax-M2.7 as a routing option when sending chat requests through the OpenCode Zen service, alongside the existing Kimi-K2.6 model. The system now uses a shared alias list and pricing table to decide which model to route to and how to charge for it, so adding this new model simply registers its name, the internal model label it maps to, and its per-token cost of 0.3 cents per million input tokens and 1.2 cents per million output tokens. If you ask for a model that isn't in that list, you'll get an error instead of it silently failing. The change is live today: the new model is accepted immediately, while unsupported names are rejected with a 400 error.

ai.title: Add Moonshot Kimi backend provider
ai.summary: New `web/src/llm-api/moonshot.ts` provider routes `moonshotai/kimi-k2.6` to `api.moonshot.ai/v1` with stream/non-stream handlers, pricing map, and `MOONSHOT_API_KEY` env var. Chat completions router inserts `useMoonshot` check before OpenCodeZen, CanopyWave, DeepSeek, Fireworks, and OpenAI. `opencode-zen.ts` removes hardcoded `MOONSHOT_KIMI_MODEL` constant, keeping alias in map. `packages/internal/src/env-schema.ts` adds optional `MOONSHOT_API_KEY`; CI defaults to 'test' in `env.ts`.

eli5.text: The assistant can now use a new AI model called Moonshot Kimi, which is now offered alongside the existing model options when someone asks for it. A new setting (MOONSHOT_API_KEY) has been added that is required to use this new model, and it is automatically set to a test value in the company's automated testing systems. When you request the Moonshot Kimi model, the software checks for it first before looking at other available models, ensuring it gets picked correctly.

ai.title: Show basher summary prompt in TUI
ai.summary: TUI agent branch previews now display the `what_to_summarize` parameter for `basher` agents when `initialPrompt` is empty. New `getAgentDisplayPrompt` utility in `cli/src/utils/agent-display.ts` handles this fallback logic. `sdk-event-handlers.ts` updated to pass `params` to agent blocks, enabling the UI to access summary details.

eli5.text: When a basher agent runs, the terminal preview now shows its summary prompt instead of leaving it blank. Developers see the basher task text displayed directly in the collapsed view, making it easier to identify what each agent is doing at a glance.

ai.title: ZeroClick ad fallback added to CLI and API
ai.summary: ZeroClick provider added as fallback for Gravity ads in CLI components and API routes. AdResponse type extended with provider and impressionIds fields; recordImpression signature changed from impUrl string to AdResponse object. ZeroClick impressions handled client-side via direct API call, bypassing server-side pixel firing; ZeroClick ads excluded from rotation cache.

eli5.text: When an ad doesn't load from the primary ad network, the command-line interface and web tools will now try a second ad provider instead of leaving a blank space. Free-tier users and visitors to the waiting room screen are the ones who'll see this backup ad; if the preferred ad isn't available, a ZeroClick ad is shown and tracked directly by the browser without going through the server. The developers added a new API key setting and told the system to keep these backup ads only for the current session so they don't get cached or reused later.

ai.title: Add DeepSeek V4 Flash to free model picker
ai.summary: DeepSeek V4 Flash added to FREEBUFF_MODELS and agent registry. New base2-free-deepseek-flash and code-reviewer-deepseek-flash agents created. Removed noAskUser flag from existing DeepSeek V4 Pro agent. Covers common constants, agent definitions, and docs.

eli5.text: You now have a new free AI model to pick from when running the assistant: DeepSeek V4 Flash, labeled as the 'Most efficient' option. When you open the model picker, alongside the existing DeepSeek V4 Pro choice, you'll see DeepSeek V4 Flash listed as available to everyone, and the tool will automatically assign it as the main agent and the code-reviewer agent for that model. The older DeepSeek V4 Pro free agent no longer asks for permission before making changes, removing that extra confirmation step that some might have expected.

ai.title: CLI code-searcher collapsed preview
ai.summary: Extracted code-search result counting and collapsed preview generation into `cli/src/utils/code-search-summary.ts`. `code-search.tsx` now delegates result counting to `countCodeSearchResults`, while `agent-branch-wrapper.tsx` uses `getCodeSearcherCollapsedPreview` to render agent-level search summaries. The new utility aggregates `searchQueries` and completed `code_search` tool outputs into a single `N searches · M results` string. Formatting and import paths in `agent-branch-wrapper.tsx` were updated to support the new helper.

eli5.text: When you run several code searches in one assistant session, the collapsed summary line now shows a single combined count like '3 searches · 12 results' instead of listing each query separately. This affects anyone who triggers multiple searches through the code-searcher assistant, because the summary text is generated in one place and both the search results display and the branch overview now read from that shared helper. If you watched the side panel while a code-searcher agent was working, you would see its collapsed preview update to that combined total rather than a longer stack of individual result counts. The change is live today.

ai.title: Limit tree-sitter project indexing memory
ai.summary: Added hard limits to tree-sitter parsing in `packages/code-map/src/parse.ts` to prevent OOM crashes during large project indexing. Introduced `CODEBUFF_MAX_PARSE_FILES` (10k), `CODEBUFF_MAX_PARSE_FILE_BYTES` (1MB), and `CODEBUFF_MAX_TOTAL_PARSE_BYTES` (500MB) environment variables with safe defaults. Refactored `sdk/src/run-state.ts` to pass a `SourceReader` callback and enforce a 1MB cap on discovered project file reads via `createDiscoveredProjectReader`. Parsing now breaks early if total byte or file count thresholds are exceeded.

eli5.text: When you open a very large project, the assistant used to try reading and analyzing every single file at once into its memory, which could crash your computer or your chat session. Now it quietly stops itself after it has collected about 10,000 files or roughly half a gigabyte of content total, and it skips any individual file larger than about a megabyte before it even tries to read it. If you watch closely while opening a big project today, you may notice it finishes scanning sooner than before, and it no longer freezes or disconnects your chat on repositories that previously overwhelmed it.

ai.title: tmux-cli added to free mode agent models
ai.summary: Added tmux-cli to FREE_MODE_AGENT_MODELS in common/src/constants/free-agents.ts. Configures the agent to use FREEBUFF_MINIMAX_MODEL_ID for command execution in free mode. Affects shared core constants and free agent definitions. Includes corresponding test coverage in common/src/__tests__/free-agents.test.ts.

eli5.text: When you use the assistant for free, it can now run command-line tools inside a split-screen terminal window instead of just a plain shell. That means you get the same tidy, organized workspace that paying users have, where each step stays visible and separate instead of scrolling past. This only applies to the free version of the assistant today.

ai.title: Update basher collapsed output preview
ai.summary: Adds `getBasherFinishedOutputPreview` to truncate basher agent output to a single line for collapsed views. `getCollapsedPreview` now uses this helper when the agent is not streaming, falling back to text or command output. This change improves readability in the CLI agent branch wrapper by respecting available width.

eli5.text: When a basher run finishes and you look at its collapsed preview, the CLI no longer shows the raw command text; instead it shows a single, width-aware line of the agent's finished output (truncated with an ellipsis if needed). You notice it only in collapsed/unstreaming branches for basher-type agents, where the preview respects the terminal width you have room for, falling back to the previous text/command output behavior when there's nothing suitable to summarize.

ai.title: DeepSeek V4 Flash labeled collecting data for training
ai.summary: Added `warning: 'Collects data for training'` to DeepSeek V4 Flash in `FREEBUFF_MODELS`. Web FAQ updated to reflect this data collection for DeepSeek V4 Flash. Scope covers `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts` and `freebuff/web/src/app/home-client.tsx`.

eli5.text: When you pick the efficient assistant on the free service, you'll now see a notice that it saves conversations to help train future versions of the assistant. The service also updated its help page so visitors can read that same data-collection fact before they start chatting. This labeling appeared on the free model list and the website's frequently asked questions at the same time.

ai.title: ChoiceAdBanner layout clamp
ai.summary: Added height: 1 and overflow: 'hidden' to the CTA/domain row in choice-ad-banner.tsx. Set wrapMode: 'none' on the domain text. Prevents banner height expansion from long domain labels. Affects CLI ad banner rendering.

eli5.text: When you use the CLI tool and it shows you a sponsorship or partnership banner at the bottom of the screen, the banner sometimes grew taller than expected if the website address shown was especially long, which could push other content out of place or make the screen look messy. Now the tool cuts off any overflowing text in that row and stops the domain name from wrapping onto its own line, so the banner keeps a fixed height no matter how long the URL is. You'd notice the banner stays compact and aligned, instead of stretching vertically and shifting nearby text.

ai.title: Simplify CLI model selector array handling
ai.summary: Removed redundant intermediate arrays in `cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx`. Directly uses `FREEBUFF_MODELS` and derives IDs via map, eliminating default-model sorting logic. Internal refactor with no behavior change.

eli5.text: The model picker in the CLI tool got internally reorganized so it no longer creates unnecessary intermediate lists just to sort them again. If you open the free model selection screen, you will see the exact same list of models in the same order as before. This is purely behind-the-scenes housekeeping that makes the code simpler without changing anything you experience.

ai.title: Freebuff 1.0.675 release
ai.summary: The CLI release package bumps to 1.0.675 in cli/release/package.json. This version ships the DeepSeek V4 Flash free model picker entry, the Moonshot Kimi backend provider, the ZeroClick ad fallback in CLI/API paths, basher summary prompt previews in the TUI, collapsed CLI code-search summaries, expanded Europe free-mode countries (FR/IT/ES/PT), the opencode/minimax-m2.7 OpenCode Zen routing addition, tmux-cli free-mode agent model support, consumed CLI auth token tracking, and tree-sitter indexing memory limits. All prior commits on 2026-05-10 and 2026-05-11 are included in this cumulative release bump.
ai.evidence: Commit [df78052c] in cli/release/package.json changes the version field from 1.0.674 to 1.0.675 in a single-line bump (diff hunk: -1.0.674 / +1.0.675).

eli5.text: This release adds a new DeepSeek V4 Flash AI model (including a note that it collects data for training), a new Moonshot Kimi backend provider, and expanded free-mode country access across Europe. You can now use the Minimax M2.7 model through OpenCode Zen routing with transparent pricing, the CLI terminal shows clearer summaries for basher agents, and code-search results are displayed as compact one-line previews. Safety and privacy improve with tracked, consumed login tokens that give clearer error messages, memory-protected large project indexing, and a ZeroClick ad fallback that bypasses server-side tracking. Upgrading brings you more AI model choices, clearer terminal summaries, broader free access, and better handling of large codebases and ads.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.86 ships new provider, models, CLI tweaks, and memory
ai.summary: Release 0.0.86 bundles the Moonshot Kimi backend provider routing moonshotai/kimi-k2.6 to api.moonshot.ai/v1, adds DeepSeek V4 Flash to the free model picker with a training-data warning, and re-adds opencode/minimax-m2.7 to OpenCode Zen routing at 0.3/1.2 per million tokens. CLI improvements include a collapsed code-search preview via cli/src/utils/code-search-summary.ts, tmux-cli available as a free-mode agent model, and basher summary prompts surfaced in the TUI. Tree-sitter project indexing is now memory-limited via CODEBUFF_MAX_PARSE_FILES, CODEBUFF_MAX_PARSE_FILE_BYTES, and CODEBUFF_MAX_TOTAL_PARSE_BYTES with safe defaults, and reused CLI auth tokens are tracked as consumed rather than deleted.
ai.evidence: Commit a4a5d358 modifies freebuff/cli/release/package.json, bumping version from 0.0.85 to 0.0.86. The single-line change is a release-bump commit.

eli5.text: This release adds a brand new AI provider backend (Moonshot Kimi), introduces the DeepSeek V4 Flash model to the free model picker, and improves how the terminal interface displays agent summaries. A new Moonshot Kimi backend now routes requests through a dedicated pathway, giving you access to that model family. DeepSeek V4 Flash is added as a fast, free option for eligible users, with a note that it collects data for training. The terminal interface now shows clearer collapsed previews for code searches and basher agent output, so you can quickly read what each agent did. Authentication tokens are now tracked as consumed instead of deleted, so the system can tell the difference between a missing login and one already used. Memory limits are enforced during large project indexing to stop the tool from crashing on huge codebases. Finally, more European countries (France, Italy, Spain, and Portugal) can now access free mode, and an ad fallback layer keeps sponsored content flowing when other providers are unavailable.

ai.title: ZeroClick ad display text fixes
ai.summary: ZeroClick ad normalization now prioritizes brand name for title and uses content or subtitle for ad text. Fixes incorrect display text caused by previous fallback logic. Affects web/src/lib/ad-providers/zeroclick.ts.

eli5.text: When a sponsored ad from ZeroClick appears, it now leads with the brand's name at the top and shows the product description or subtitle as the supporting text underneath, instead of mixing those details around as it did before. You'd notice that ads now display the company name first, making them easier to recognize at a glance. This fix corrects the previous logic that sometimes showed the wrong text in either the headline or the body of the ad.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.87 release bumps package version from 0.0.86
ai.summary: Version 0.0.87 increments the Freebuff package version from 0.0.86, bundling the same-day release updates including ZeroClick ad display text normalization changes in `web/src/lib/ad-providers/zeroclick.ts`. The ZeroClick normalization now prioritizes brand name for the title and uses content or subtitle for ad text, fixing display issues caused by the previous fallback logic. This version bump ships the ad normalization fix alongside previously released model, provider, and CLI improvements detailed in the surrounding commits and release notes.
ai.evidence: Modified file `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` shows version field bumped from 0.0.86 to 0.0.87 in a release-bump commit (6920f0c3) on 2026-05-11.

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.0.87 improves how sponsored ads are displayed in your feed so they look cleaner and more reliable. When ads load, the title now highlights the brand name you might recognize, and the main text under it pulls from the ad's content or subtitle instead of awkward placeholder info. This means you will see fewer glitches in ad wording and a smoother experience when browsing, making sponsored content easier to read and understand.
